display: Retired music teacher who directs a thirty-voice community choir in a church basement in Scarborough, Toronto. For years we rehearsed with a cheap keyboard.

signals.text: We have only three tenors, and I am rewriting parts down an octave to cope. I would love a few more tenors or baritones who can read music.
I am recruiting singers for the Christmas concert on December 13. We need at least 24 and have about 14 confirmed.
A couple of sopranos moved away this autumn, and the choir is leaner than it was in June.
Our budget comes from bake sales and donations, and every extra cost is a real decision.
People arrive tired on Thursday nights, but they keep coming. I am looking for ways to keep rehearsals warm and worth the trip.
A kind donation gave us a good upright piano, and now the rehearsal room barely fits it. The altos sit sideways.
Our board has said no more instruments or donations because of fire code and room capacity. I accept the decision, but I'm still a little sad about it.
Four Christmas pieces use brass, and one of our lenders is eighty and unsure about the high notes. I am transposing parts so he can keep playing.
I am looking at the whole December plan: eight pieces plus a carol sing-along, with a brass rehearsal on October 22 and a concert budget meeting on October 31.
My evenings outside Thursday rehearsal are limited right now because of family commitments at home.
I have been wondering who could eventually take the baton, and how long I will keep directing.
I am teaching myself sourdough with a moody starter named Gerald. The loaves are getting better, but the crumb is still gummy.

offers.text: Thirty-two years of teaching choral and instrumental music in Ontario public schools, including rehearsal planning, warm-ups and managing mixed-ability groups.
I can adapt choral parts to the voices you have: transposing, rewriting parts down an octave, and simplifying for weaker sections.
I have a large library of SATB arrangements, mostly photocopied over the decades, and I can suggest repertoire for community choirs.
I direct a welcoming community choir with singers aged 19 to 84 and mixed abilities. Beginners are welcome on Thursday evenings.
I can run a short coaching session or workshop for another community or church choir on rehearsing, blend or sight-reading.
Our choir sings at Christmas, Easter and funerals, and we can provide music for a memorial service.
I have access to a borrowed brass quartet for concerts, arranged through a retired trumpeter in a neighbouring parish.
I know a retired engineer who can advise on practical problems such as room layout and building constraints.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm a tenor in my fifties. I haven't sung in a choir for years, but I read music and live in Scarborough. Do you have room for me?
catchers.can: Invite them to a Thursday 7pm rehearsal and give them a part and a folder. We need tenors badly.
catchers.confirm: Can you attend Thursday evening rehearsals in Scarborough from now until the December 13 concert?

catchers.hypo: I'm a retired brass player. I'm a bit rusty and my range isn't what it was, but I'd love to play in a group again.
catchers.can: Transpose parts into a comfortable key, as I did for my trumpeter, and add them to the Christmas programme if the brass line has room.
catchers.confirm: Are you happy to play from parts transposed into a comfortable key and to rehearse with the choir before the concert?

catchers.hypo: My father died last year, and I want to honour him with music. Could a choir dedicate a piece to him at a service or concert?
catchers.can: Dedicate a piece at the Christmas concert or sing at a memorial. A parishioner gave us a piano in memory of her husband, so I know how much that can mean.
catchers.confirm: Do you want a piece dedicated in someone's memory within a service or concert, rather than a paid performance?

catchers.hypo: I'm a music teacher starting a community choir. Do you have advice on repertoire, part-writing for a weak section, or running rehearsals?
catchers.can: Share my SATB library, suggest repertoire and give practical advice on rewriting parts and structuring rehearsals.
catchers.confirm: Are you working with an amateur or community choir rather than a professional ensemble?

catchers.hypo: I'm a young conductor looking for a mentor and a real choir to work with. Could I shadow rehearsals and take part of one?
catchers.can: Offer a place beside me in rehearsal and some time on the podium. This also gives me a way to think about who might one day carry the choir on.
catchers.confirm: Can you commit to regular Thursday evenings over several months rather than a single visit?

catchers.hypo: I'm a structural or building-safety engineer. I'd happily look at how a basement rehearsal room could be laid out for a piano and a choir of thirty.
catchers.can: Introduce them through my husband, a retired engineer, who can talk through room layout and constraints.
catchers.confirm: Is your offer about advice on layout or safety within the existing space, rather than adding furniture or equipment?

catchers.hypo: I'm learning sourdough and my starter is sulking. The crust is great but the crumb is gummy. Any tips?
catchers.can: Trade notes. I keep a log of times and temperatures for my starter, as I would for a choir warm-up.
catchers.confirm: Are you a home baker comparing notes rather than someone selling a bread course or product?

forbids.text: No more instruments, furniture or donations in the church basement. It is at fire-code capacity.
I cannot add chairs or singers beyond what the room safely holds.
I have no budget for fees. The choir runs on bake sales and donations.
I am not available on most evenings other than Thursday rehearsal.
I only work in the Toronto area, mainly Scarborough.

projects.name: Christmas concert, December 13
projects.text: Eight pieces plus a carol sing-along, with a brass quartet on four of them. We need more singers, especially tenors.

policy.t1: When there is a real sign of fit, I will share details of the Christmas concert plan, the Yamaha donation, the room capacity and the board's decision.
policy.t2: Once there is trust and I know who you are, I will share my personal worries about the choir's future and who might eventually carry it on.
policy.never: Medical details of anyone in my family and any family finances.
